text:
marta: Uploaded the nsys dump from the failing batch run (seqlen spikes). Seen a 30% p90 regression when KV prefetch + large batches coincide. perfetto link in the repo.
alex: looked at the timeline — kernel selection looks fine but theres a ~12ms gap between KV load and attention kernel start.
sam: is that the KV cache miss path or just a scheduling hole? :thinking_face:
li: I think it's the KV prefetch path hitting the slow memcpy path on our vmem page alignment. nvtx shows a wide range labeled `kv_prefetch` then idle.
jordan: can you paste the nvtx snippet? curious about naming. we've been inconsistent with ranges which makes aggregation painful.
marta: heres the relevant excerpt from the trace (nsys -> perfetto):
```
NVTX Range: request/req-42/start
NVTX Range: req-42/kv_prefetch (tags: cache_miss=1, size=512KB)
NVTX Range: kernel/select:attention_short
NVTX Range: req-42/kernel/attention_short/launch
NVTX Range: req-42/kv_apply (tags: prefetch_hit=0)
NVTX Range: request/req-42/end
```
alex: two quick notes: 1) naming is too verbose for the hot path (costly to emit metadata), 2) we need stable keys for grouping across traces.
sam: proposal: short hierarchical names + attributes when needed. e.g. `req:42:kv_prefetch` and push attrs as nvtx payloads: `{hit:0, size:512}`.
li: agree but payloads increase overhead. For high QPS we want a cheap boolean tag. What about sampling only KV detail ranges at 1% and always emit kernel ranges?
jordan: we should differentiate span granularity: per-request high-level spans (always) + sampled detailed spans (kv internals, memcpy). That lowers overhead while keeping signal.
marta: re: sampling strategy — I tried a burst-aware sampler: sample when latency deviates > 2x from rolling p50 OR probabilistic base rate 0.5%. Captures regressions without lots of noise.
alex: interesting. did you test it with steady traffic? false positives? prefetch noise?
marta: steady traffic: sampling rate remained ~0.6% with ~99% of traces being high-level only. During the regression window it shot to ~12% automatically.
ci-bot: perf upload complete: https://perfetto.local/trace/1987654321
sam: nice. For nvtx names Id propose the following canonical pattern:
- Top-level: `req/<short-id>` (always)
- Kernel: `k/<name>` (always)
- Sampled internal: `s/kv` or `s/memcpy` (sampled)
- Attributes: small set of standardized keys: `hit`, `seq`, `size_kb`

Example:
```
NVTX push: "req/3f2"
NVTX push: "k/attn_short"
NVTX pop
NVTX push: "s/kv"  // emitted only when sampled
  payload: {hit:0,seq:1024,size_kb:512}
NVTX pop
NVTX pop
```
li: thats concise. My one worry is correlating kernels to model layers when we do kernel-level aggregation across runs (we rely on kernel name + seq distribution). Maybe add `seq` as an attribute on kernel ranges as well.
alex: yeah add `seq` to `k/<name>` when available. But avoid adding `req` id into kernel name — keep ids out of aggregation keys.
jordan: about implementation: we should implement a tiny sampler in runtime that runs before NVTX emission. Config flags: `nvtx_sampling.base_rate`, `nvtx_sampling.dynamic_burst_threshold`, `nvtx_emit_kernel_seq_attr`.
marta: I have a draft patch that adds a sampling hook in RequestContext and toggles emission of `s/*` ranges. Also added a small fast-path to tag `k/*` with `seq` when seq<=2048 (fits in 16 bits).
sam: can you open a PR? include a micro-benchmark for NVTX overhead (QPS with and w/o sampling) so ops can justify enabling by default.
marta: will do. PR link when ready.
alex: one more ask: add a mapping table in the runtime docs for canonical short names to long descriptions. That way perf folks can run queries like `group by k/attn_short seq=...`.
jordan: agreed. also add a small script `trace_normalize.py` to collapse `req/<id>` into `req/_` for aggregation.
li: tiny note: be careful with payload serialization on older drivers — nvtx payload size matters. Keep it to ints.
sam: overall +1. This sampling + naming combo should make hotspot detection less noisy and reduce perf tracing overhead.
marta: thanks team — I'll land the sampler PR and follow up with the perfbench numbers and the perfetto link. :rocket:
